name: Upholstered or wooden bed with a headboard
tagline: Fabric or wood headboard, two side rails, and slats. The headboard bolts are the fiddly part.
peopleNote: Genuinely a two-person job. The headboard is heavy and awkward and needs holding upright while you bolt it.

tools.why: The headboard bolts are often hex-head and far easier with a wrench than the little Allen key.
You will be looking into dark pockets behind fabric for hidden bolt holes.

before: Build it in the bedroom with the door closed behind you. This never fits through a doorway assembled.
Lay the headboard face-down on the bed's cardboard or a blanket. Fabric picks up every bit of grit from a bare floor.
Get the mattress out of the room entirely if you can, or stand it in the hallway.
safety: Never let the headboard stand unsupported while only partly bolted. It will fall, and it is heavy.
Slats must all be present and secured. A missing slat concentrates all your weight onto its neighbors.

steps.title: Lay the headboard face-down on something soft
steps.say: Put the headboard face-down on a blanket or the flattened box. You will be working on its back, and fabric scuffs.
do: Face-down, padded surface
Legs or bolt plates pointing up at you
Have a second person steady it
steps.watch: Do not drag an upholstered headboard across carpet. It pulls threads.

steps.title: Find the hidden bolt holes
steps.say: On upholstered beds the bolt holes are often behind a flap of fabric or inside a dark pocket. Shine a light and feel for the metal plate.
do: Look for a seam or flap you can lift
Feel through the fabric for a hard metal plate
Shine a light directly into the pocket
steps.tip: Push the fabric aside with a finger rather than cutting anything. The holes are always there, just buried.
steps.watch: Never cut fabric to find a hole. Check the manual's diagram again instead.

steps.title: Attach the side rails to the headboard, loosely
steps.say: Bring one side rail up to the headboard and start its bolts with washers. Finger-tight only. The frame needs to move to find its shape.
do: Washer between bolt head and bracket, every time
Thread by hand first, then a couple of turns with the key
Do both side rails before tightening anything
steps.tip: Left and right rails are usually different. Check for L and R markings, often stamped or stickered on the inside face.

steps.title: Bring in the foot rail and close the rectangle
steps.say: The foot rail joins the two side rails and completes the rectangle. Bolt it finger-tight too. Now you have a frame you can square up.
do: Line up the brackets, start every bolt by hand
Keep everything loose
Check the rectangle looks roughly right
steps.watch: If a bolt refuses to start, the rail is upside down. Brackets usually only fit one way round.

steps.title: Fit the center support and its legs
steps.say: The center rail runs head to foot down the middle and carries most of the load. Bolt it in and screw its legs down until they touch the floor.
do: Bolt both ends to the head and foot rails
Screw the center legs in
Make sure each leg actually contacts the floor
steps.watch: A center leg hovering a quarter inch above the floor does nothing. Thread it down until it bears weight.

steps.title: Stand it up and square the frame
steps.say: With two people, lift the frame upright onto its legs. Measure both diagonals and nudge until they match.
do: Lift together, from the rails not the fabric
Measure corner to corner both ways
Push the long corner until the numbers agree
steps.tip: Squaring a bed matters more than people think. It is why one side of the mattress ends up sitting proud of the frame.

steps.title: Tighten every bolt, twice around
steps.say: Now tighten everything firmly, working around the frame. Then do a second lap, because the first lap loosens things.
do: Headboard bolts first, they carry the most stress
Then side rails, then foot, then center
Second full lap
steps.tip: Firm, not gorilla-tight. You are clamping steel to wood and you can crush the wood.

steps.title: Lay and secure the slats
steps.say: Drop each slat into its clip or onto its ledge, spacing them evenly. Screw down the ones the manual tells you to.
do: Even spacing, head to foot
Push each one fully into its clip
Screw or clip the end slats so the set cannot migrate
steps.watch: Count the slats against the manual. A bed short one slat will develop a dip exactly where you sleep.

steps.title: Sit on each corner, then make the bed
steps.say: Sit heavily on each corner and the middle. Listen for creaks and look for flex. Fix anything now, before the mattress hides it all.
do: Sit on each corner and the center
Rock side to side
Chase any creak to its bolt and tighten
steps.tip: A creak that appears a month in is almost always a bolt that settled. Keep the Allen key in your nightstand drawer.

fixes.q: I cannot find the bolt holes on the headboard
fixes.a: They are behind the fabric. Lift any flap along the bottom edge, or feel for a hard metal plate and part the fabric with your fingers. Check the manual diagram for roughly how far from the edge. Never cut.

fixes.q: The headboard wobbles side to side
fixes.a: The headboard bolts are not tight, or washers were left out. Washers spread the load and stop the bolt pulling through. Take it apart far enough to add them.

fixes.q: The side rails are different and I bolted on the wrong one
fixes.a: Easy fix. Loosen it off, swap sides, re-bolt. Check inside faces for an L or R sticker.

fixes.q: There is a gap between the mattress and the headboard
fixes.a: The frame is out of square, or the slats have drifted toward the foot. Square the diagonals and push the slat set back up to the head.

fixes.q: The bed creaks every time I move
fixes.a: Full tightening lap first. Then check for wood-on-wood contact at the slat ends and stick on felt pads. Also make sure the frame is not touching the wall — that knock sounds exactly like a frame creak.
